,[H-1] Lack of slippage protection leads to loss of protocol funds The protocol is missing slippage protection in two key areas. First, when a Liquidity Vault (LV) token holder redeems early, the `swapExactTokensForTokens` function is called with `amountOutMin` set to `0`. Second, when the protocol removes liquidity from an Automated Market Maker (AMM), the `removeLiquidity` function is called with `amountAMin` and `amountBMin` both set to `0`. This allows an attacker to manipulate prices through front-running, causing a loss of funds.  [H-2] FlashSwapRouter functions return incorrect values The `FlashSwapRouter::emptyReserve()` and `FlashSwapRouter::emptyReservePartial()` functions incorrectly return the *remaining* reserve amount instead of the amount that was emptied. This flawed logic causes downstream calculations to fail, which can prevent users from redeeming their tokens and result in locked funds.  [H-3] LV token holders receive disproportional fees The fee distribution mechanism is flawed because it does not account for the length of time a user has provided liquidity. A user who deposits funds just before fees are distributed receives the same proportional share as a long-term provider, allowing new depositors to claim an unfair share of rewards.  [H-4] Incorrect accounting for redeemAmount due to missing exchange rate The protocol incorrectly accounts for redeemed assets by failing to apply the exchange rate. When CT and DS tokens are redeemed, the amount is added to the RA balance without conversion, leading to inaccurate accounting and affecting the funds available for withdrawal.  [H-6] Users can steal funds due to incorrect balance reduction in `VaultPoolLib::redeem()` When a user redeems an expired LV token for an amount greater than their initial request, the `__redeemExcessFromAmmPool()` function is called but fails to decrease the withdrawal pool balances (`raBalance` and `paBalance`). This error allows the funds to be double-counted in the next issuance, inflating the exchange rate and enabling users to withdraw more funds than they are entitled to.  [H-11] Untracked Pegged Asset (PA) leads to stuck funds The `VaultPoolLib::reserve()` function incorrectly handles the Pegged Asset (PA) The portion of PA allocated to the AMM is not accounted for in subsequent functions, causing it to become untracked and permanently stuck in the Vault.  [M-4] Attacker can set the initial AMM pair ratio When a new AMM pair is created, the protocol does not add initial liquidity, leaving the pool empty and vulnerable [cite: 1495-1496]. An attacker can front-run the first deposit and set a malicious price ratio, which the protocol will then use for subsequent deposits, creating an arbitrage opportunity that drains value from the system.  [M-5] Withdrawing all LV before expiry locks funds in the Vault If all users redeem their LV tokens before a series expires, the total supply of LV tokens becomes zero. After expiry, a function to liquidate remaining assets will revert with a division-by-zero error because it tries to calculate a rate based on the zero supply of LV tokens, causing all remaining funds in the Vault to be permanently stuck.  [M-7] Unchecked return values when adding liquidity lead to locked funds When adding liquidity to an AMM, the protocol does not check the return values to confirm the actual amount of tokens used. Due to rounding, small amounts of tokens (dust) may not be used by the AMM and are left in the contract.
